exampleNotice: ILLUSTRATIVE EXAMPLE. Every row below is invented for public demonstration of the SCOPE workflow. These are not extracts from any real system and describe no real organisation, product or plan.
grain: One row per product family, per closed planning period.
note: Held separately from the plan on purpose. In standard demand planning, actuals arrive from order or shipment history, not from the planning system, so they are a different source with a different owner and a different arrival date. Keeping them apart is what makes forecast accuracy, bias and forecast value add honest measures rather than self-assessment.
why_separate: If actuals lived in the plan table, a plan edit could silently change a measured accuracy result. Separation means the scoreboard cannot be edited by the team being scored.
closed_periods_only: Only periods whose demand is complete appear here. Open periods are deliberately absent, because comparing a forecast against a partial actual overstates error.

rowNotes.DEMO-EDGE / 2025-Q3: Judgement moved the forecast further from the actual than the statistical baseline was. This is the case that makes forecast value add negative, and it is included deliberately - a demo where human judgement always wins would not be a useful demo.
rowNotes.DEMO-STANDARD / 2025-Q4: Judgement moved the forecast towards the actual. Positive value add.
rowNotes.DEMO-PREMIUM / 2025-Q3: Both forecasts under-called the period, so bias is negative for both.

caveat: These rows demonstrate how accuracy, bias and forecast value add are derived and traced. They are not evidence that any source has been quality-checked.
